thematicAnalysis: True sentience (sentire) demands an immediate, somatic immersion in existence rather than an analytical retreat or postponement of vitality (carpe diem). Across aesthetic ecstasy (frisson) and communal, outward-beaming pride (kvell), subjective experience is sanctified through visceral, present-tense emotional communion.
quote: We should consider every day lost on which we have not danced at least once.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
synthesisNote: Nietzsche crystallizes the imperative to convert raw perceptual capacity (sentire) into uninhibited, immediate engagement (carpe diem), demanding that each moment culminate in somatic and shared ecstasy (frisson and kvell).
